CORRECTION, and a general caution about sha citations on a rebased branch: earlier drafts of this file, and the message of commit ac35e5c02b, cite the payload as living at commits a1b77e3265 / 1b7906526b / 3e926d2744. Those shas were real when written but are pre-rebase orphans -- the merge lane rebases this branch, so they are not reachable from main and `git show <sha>:<path>` will fail outright once gc prunes them. Commit messages are immutable history and are left as-is; this note is the correction of record. Any durability pin on a not-yet-merged branch must be a repo-relative path plus a content hash, never a same-branch commit sha. The same caveat applies to the git_sha field above (896ece8983): it faithfully records what HEAD pointed at when the sweep ran and is a run-environment measurement, not a recovery pin, so it is likewise not expected to be reachable from main.

ROOT CAUSE, measured not guessed: the agent sandbox denies file CREATION in ~/.mem0. A probe from the same environment shows open('~/.mem0/.write-probe','w') raises PermissionError [Errno 13] while the existing history.db still accepts BEGIN IMMEDIATE. SQLite cannot create its rollback journal in that directory and therefore reports 'attempt to write a readonly database'. The file itself is mode 0644, uid 1000, os.access(W_OK)=True -- so this is NOT a filesystem permissions defect on the db.

CONSEQUENCE FOR OPERATORS: --apply must not be run from inside a sandboxed agent session. The Qdrant mutation is a network call to localhost:6333 and succeeds, while mem0's local SQLite history write is blocked -- so the sandbox splits a delete-then-re-add exactly down the middle and produces partial mutations. Re-running the sweep will NOT recover 7d073281; the runbook is explicit that a record in this state must not be re-swept.
